claim: First live run of the new local gate (npm run check:formation, five local node processes, HEAD 103786ef3 + this candidate, 2026-09-05T19:44Z): FAIL with reason node_ready_lease_incomplete. The seed was NOT starved (13 gaps, 3186 ms unexplained of a 63.8 s formation window, max gap 6.3 s), yet the critical-topology settling blocker logged 138 settle waits with up to five nodes unready and the seed itself unready in 131 of them, the priority spread gap went 12 -> 9 -> 8 and then sat in critical_spread_open for 54 observations, and schema admission timed out. So the ready-lease-incomplete reading reproduces locally without event-loop starvation: the seed classifies ITSELF as an ACTIVE node without a current ready lease. The GCP failure adds starvation on top; the lease reading is the common owner.
rulesOut: Do not attribute the formation blocker to seed starvation alone; the local reproduction has none. Do not weaken the gate's budget to make this run pass.

attempt.hypothesis: Release process simplification: RELEASE.md defines a deterministic release exit (ci gate green on the exact SHA, clean release content at origin/main, agreeing versions plus a cut changelog section, no existing tag) evaluated by npm run release:preflight, which prints the tag commands and never tags; the release-0-2 verification machinery (scenario runners, receipt recorders, derivation, constants, candidate identity, test, package scripts, tool descriptions) is deleted and the 0.2 epic records the supersession; CHANGELOG notes return to [Unreleased] with the measured formation state and the release-notes wiring test accepts an uncut version; the demo records formation phase timing, a --formation-only mode reporting under its own scenario, and a machine-readable formationVerdict (seed gaps in the formation window with hot sites, ready-lease settle waits, last observed critical spread, admission end state, causal chain) derived by examples/service-data-affinity/formation-verdict.js; npm run health:formation appends one verdict record per run to data/formation-health/trend.ndjson and renders the trend, a scheduled formation-health workflow runs it on the GCP runner; npm run check:formation is the local seed-starvation gate; the pre-push comment states the one-full-corpus-per-head rule.

Release process simplification (fresh attempt after the receipt existed): RELEASE.md deterministic release exit + npm run release:preflight; release-0-2 verification machinery deleted with the epic supersession recorded; CHANGELOG notes under [Unreleased] with the measured formation state; demo formation timing, --formation-only mode and machine-readable formationVerdict; npm run health:formation trend + scheduled formation-health workflow; npm run check:formation local seed-starvation gate; pre-push comment states one full corpus per head.
